text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Top Pakistani negotiators claimed satisfactory progress in talks with the IMF over a new economic reform package.

- Pakistan's Chief Justice Syed Sajjad Ali Shah, at the request of the federal government, has nominated Supreme Court judge Nasir Aslam Zahid, as chairman of the inquiry tribunal probing the murder of Murtaza Bhutto.
- Pakistan urged the United Nations Security Council to adopt a resolution on Afghanistan seeking immediate cessation of armed hostilities and imposition of arms embargo on all sides.
- The day-long power failure in the port city of Karachi, which had disrupted civic life on Wednesday, dragged on to Thursday as many parts remained without electricity and water.
- President Farooq Leghari was to leave for Tashkent on Friday on a three-day state visit to Uzbekistan.
- Sugar prices on the local wholesale market soared to a new peak of 21.25 rupees on heavy buying triggered by news of delay in starting the crushing season.
- A government commission will inquire into non-performing loans in banks and financial institutions from January 1980 with particular reference to loans of 10 million rupees or more.
- The United States may impose trade sanctions if Pakistan does not abandon mega-projects with Iran in the energy sector.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto met President Farooq Leghari to discuss postings and transfers of government officials.
- The situation in Pakistan is expected to take a decisive turn in the next few days due to economic, political, judicial and administrative crises in the country.
- Investment Minister Asif Ali Zardari left for Britain to prepare for an investment conference on October 28 in London.
